sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: World Trade Organization WTO Membership, effective 10 May 2012
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations PACER Plus, in force 13 December 2020

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987, as amended; Companies Act 2001; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2018; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2011; Beneficial Ownership and Registered Agent Regulations issued by the Samoa Registrar of Companies under the International Companies Act; obligations deriving from FATF and the Asia/Pacific Group on Money Laundering.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport office, law enforcement authority or notary public in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if originating in an Apostille Contracting State, otherwise Consular Legalization through the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO declaration and certificate of identity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Samoa registered agent or notary public in the beneficiary's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or Consular Legalization when required for onward filing outside Samoa; internal verification accepted for Samoan Registry requirements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified proof of residential address for directors, shareholders and beneficial owners, dated within the last 90 days
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank, utility company or government revenue office, with notarial certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation and memorandum of association of corporate shareholder, together with corporate chain and register of directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating company registry and corporate secretary of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille or Consular Legalization as appropriate to the originating jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney authorizing the Samoa registered agent and law firm to file the incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the grantor's jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners and authorized signatories against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit consolidated list, United Nations Security Council sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions list, Australian DFAT consolidated list, and the World Bank Listing of Ineligible Firms. Politically Exposed Persons PEP status is to be identified using a risk-based approach for foreign, domestic and international organization PEPs, with enhanced due diligence and senior management approval required for any PEP or sanctions-related hit. Ongoing transaction monitoring is required where the Samoa International Company opens a bank account or uses regulated payment rails such as Stripe Billing or Wise B2B.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Companies Registry Online Services, operated by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour MCIL, Companies and Intellectual Property Division
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in English or Samoan. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin script for registry indexing and statutory name matching. The name must not be misleading, offensive, contrary to public policy, or so similar to an existing registered name as to create confusion. An International Company name must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.' and must be shown in that form in its constitutional documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: International unless specifically approved by the Registrar or expressly permitted under the International Companies Act
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may apply to the Registrar for a single extension of up to 30 additional days before the initial reservation expiry. If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar within 14 days of the rejection notice, setting out the grounds of distinctiveness and producing search results showing no identical or arguably confusing prior registration. If the Registrar confirms rejection, a further appeal may be lodged with the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 30 days. Legal counsel should be engaged where the contested name carries significant brand value.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Prohibited as a substitute for the statutory registered office. A Samoa International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa, typically at the premises of a licensed registered agent. Shared office and administrative support facilities used by the agent are permissible, but a mail-forwarding address or remote virtual office does not satisfy the statutory substance mandate. The enterprise SaaS entity may continue to operate sales, engineering and software development activities from remote locations without affecting the Samoan registered office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, quantified at approximately 5% annual probability for a standard low-risk B2B enterprise SaaS international company. Unannounced physical inspections are not routine; they may occur only where the Registrar, Financial Intelligence Unit or relevant regulator has a reasonable suspicion of AML/CFT non-compliance, sanctions involvement, misrepresentation of business activity, or where the registered agent is the subject of a compliance audit.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name search and prioritization for two candidate names
Government incorporation fee for an International Company under the International Companies Act 1987
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Samoa
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff under International Companies Act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed registered agent and physical registered office, first annual fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Samoa registered agent and corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Samoa international company maintenance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of UBO declaration, director consents, proof of identity and proof of address
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in shareholder jurisdiction and Samoa registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notary tariff and market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization fees for UBO and corporate document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority in document origin such as Secretary of State, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or Samoan consular official

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance setup including PEP, OFAC, UN, EU and domestic sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent AML compliance team or external compliance consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee, prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence and pre-incorporation opinion covering UBO piercing, name clearance, corporate structure and Samoan regulatory fitness
Courier and expedited filing logistics for certified certificates from offshore jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: International courier service and MCIL priority filing desk

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (No. 15 of 1987, as amended), ss. 6-12 (incorporation procedure), s. 12 (name restrictions), s. 27 (registered office), s. 38 (registered agent), ss. 43-56 (directors and officers), Schedule 1 (prescribed fees)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of an International Company (Form IC-1) together with annexed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow bank account required. Standard International Company charter adopts US$100,000 authorized capital divided into 1,000,000 shares at US$0.10 par value; the subscription price is payable at allotment in cash or non-cash consideration, and shares may be issued with par or no par value under the Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that: 1. The subscription list of shares is approved, and the authorized share capital of US$100,000 is allotted to the subscribers at par in accordance with the Memorandum and Articles of Association. 2. The registered office located at [Address], Apia, Samoa is adopted, and the licensed registered agent is confirmed as agent for service of process as required by the International Companies Act 1987. 3. [Director] is appointed Director and President, with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and bind the Company. 4. [Secretary] is appointed Corporate Secretary. 5. All pre-incorporation contracts executed on behalf of the Company are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL Companies Registry (application submitted through a licensed Samoa registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the licensed registered agent. The proposed name must end in 'Limited' or 'Ltd', must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing domestic or international company, must not imply government patronage, and must not be contrary to public policy or the Act. Two alternative names may be submitted in the same application to expedite clearance.
required_dossiers: Consent of the proposed registered agent
Certified copy of KYC identification of the proposed beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit alternative names without additional fee; apply in writing to the Registrar for reconsideration; where refusal is allegedly without statutory basis, seek judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Licensed Registered Agent and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ICSP licensed by MCIL; Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a registered agent services agreement with a Samoa-licensed agent maintaining a physical office in Apia. The agent supplies the registered office address and accepts service of process. Complete the agent's consent form for annexure to the incorporation application. The agent performs the mandatory AML/KYC due diligence screening of all shareholders and beneficial owners.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as registered agent (statutory form)
KYC/AML dossier: passport, proof of residential address, bank and professional references of each ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointed agent withdraws consent, appoint a substitute licensed agent and file a notice of change of registered agent under s. 38(5) of the Act prior to submitting the incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Constituent Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent; Samoa notary public or foreign notary / Samoan consular officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, executed by each subscriber and countersigned by the registered agent. Subscribers executing outside Samoa must have signatures attested by a notary public or a Samoan diplomatic or consular officer, with the notarial certificate annexed. Ensure the articles name the initial directors and permit the issuance of share certificates.
required_dossiers: Notarially certified signature page of each subscriber
Statutory declaration of compliance by the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Registrar identifies omissions or statutory inconsistencies, amend the constituent documents and re-execute the corrected signature pages; the statutory declaration may be re-submitted by the registered agent on the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Application and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the registered agent's consent, and the statutory declaration of compliance. Pay the government incorporation fee of US$150 or the WST equivalent at the MCIL cashier or by bank transfer. Upon compliance, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the official seal, dated as of filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond in writing to the Registrar's requisition letter within 21 days, cure the stated defects, and re-file; the first corrective re-filing attracts no additional fee; persistent refusal may be challenged by judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance, Share Issuance, and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First Board of Directors; licensed commercial bank in Samoa; MCIL Business Licence Office (only if physical presence in Samoa)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or adopt written resolutions, passing the First Board Resolution approving the allotment of shares, adoption of the registered office, and appointment of officers. Issue share certificates and record entries in the register of members and register of directors. Open a corporate bank account by presenting the Certificate of Incorporation, board resolution, and beneficial owner KYC. If physical operations commence, file the Business Licence application.
required_dossiers: Share certificates and register of members
Corporate banking account application and KYC pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Defects in share allotment or officer appointment are cured by supplementary board resolution or corrective filing with the Registrar; a bank account rejection is remedied by submitting enhanced due diligence information or by selecting an alternate licensed bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business Licence Office, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) under the Business Licenses Act 1998
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (General - Information Technology and Software Services) applicable only where the International Company maintains physical premises or employs staff in Samoa

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Assessment and Review Committee (EARC), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), jointly with the Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Registration (Low Impact). Office-only SaaS operations with no industrial plant are processed by registration rather than a Full EIA Report; a registered-office-only International Company with no physical premises is exempt from EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or point-source discharges; office wastewater discharged only to municipal sewerage in compliance with the Water Resources Management Act 2008; negligible VOC emissions from office operations; waste electrical and electronic equipment (e-waste) routed to licensed recyclers under the Waste Management Act 2005.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and annual inspection by the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA); building occupancy certificate from PUMA based on the National Building Code structural load requirements; workplace registration and occupational safety compliance clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1997 administered by the MCIL Labour Division for any Samoan office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue – Samoa Tax Administration (official portal: Samoa Tax Administration via mof.gov.ws)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: International Companies are not automatically required to obtain a Samoan TIN because they are tax-exempt offshore entities. If the International Company makes any domestic taxable supplies or voluntarily seeks a TIN for banking, invoicing, or CRS purposes, it must file Form IRD-TIN with Samoa Tax Administration, submit the International Company registration certificate and directors register, and receive a TIN/IRD number. For purely offshore B2B SaaS revenue, no domestic tax return filing is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections are available. The International Company is conclusively treated as a tax-exempt offshore entity under the International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa); if it engages in domestic taxable activity, standard VAGST and domestic TIN obligations apply, but this is a factual trigger rather than an entity-level tax election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual taxable turnover for domestic supplies; International Companies deriving only offshore B2B SaaS revenue fall outside this threshold and are not required to register for VAGST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API reporting, or digital stamping mandate is currently applicable in Samoa. Taxpayers must issue VAGST invoices in a form acceptable to Samoa Tax Administration, retain complete records, and ensure invoices clearly identify the supplier, recipient, description of supply, and VAGST treatment. Zero-rated export invoices must carry a supporting export declaration or service export substantiation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods physically exported from Samoa and to services supplied to a non-resident customer if the services are not performed in Samoa and are not otherwise used or consumed in Samoa. For B2B Enterprise SaaS, the International Company may claim 0% VAGST when the customer is a foreign enterprise, payment is received from outside Samoa, the software/platform is accessed offshore, and no local Samoan establishment is the user or beneficiary.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (where physical goods are involved; for cross-border SaaS this is substituted by a service export declaration and client contract)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (for physical exports; for digital services: signed B2B service agreement and offshore usage/service delivery records)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT confirmation showing receipt of foreign sales proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are scrutinised by Samoa Tax Administration through document review and audit. Misstated or fraudulent export claims trigger retrospective VAGST assessments at 10% on the undeclared supply, late payment penalties, evasion penalties of up to 100% of the tax undercharged, and possible prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 2015, including fines and imprisonment for deliberate tax fraud. An International Company without substantiating contracts, offshore payment evidence, and customer non-residency proof cannot sustain a 0% rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa) is the sole exchange-control authority, operating under the Exchange Control Act 1973 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1974, with delegated execution via banks licensed as Authorized Dealers in Samoa. The Financial Services Authority of Samoa separately administers the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) and supervises the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is a restricted offshore currency; current-account transactions are generally free through authorized dealers with documentary support, while capital-account remittances (equity injection, shareholder loans, distributions) require CBS prior approval or an applicable exemption. The WS_IC International Company is statutorily prohibited from offering services to, or transacting with, Samoan residents and from operating in WST; therefore all treasury flows are USD-denominated in foreign-currency accounts, eliminating convertibility risk. Profit-remittance analysis: the IC, being incorporated under the International Companies Act and managed and controlled outside Samoa, is a non-resident company under the Income Tax Act 2012; dividends paid from non-resident-source SaaS revenue carry no Samoan income tax or withholding tax, provided the non-resident management and economic substance position is documented.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa's Exchange Control framework requires domestic exporters to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days of shipment and historically applies a mandatory partial conversion (commonly 15-25%) into WST. The WS_IC SaaS enterprise is not treated as an exporter of goods by CBS practice because services are rendered entirely outside Samoa and settled in USD; the IC is granted a standing exemption permitting 100% retention of USD in its designated foreign-currency operating account. No conversion or surrender order applies where funds never enter the WST clearing system; however, the authorized dealer must file quarterly inflow aggregates with CBS under the External Transactions Reporting regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Multi-Currency Operational Account; USD Capital Escrow/Investment Account established separately for equity injection funds
USD Corporate Foreign-Currency Settlement Account for high-volume treasury clearing and interbank cover
USD Offshore IC Settlement Account with segregated client-funds sub-ledger and Vostro-compatible wiring instructions

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility for the WS_IC is Medium for USD/EUR receivable collection via Stripe Billing and Wise Business, and Low for any WST-denominated or Samoa-resident-facing service. Samoa has no dedicated EMI licensing regime, and the CBS Payment and Settlement Systems Regulations require a licence for activities touching the domestic WST system; offshore EMIs that settle only in foreign currency into a licensed Samoa bank account do not require a Samoan PSP licence. Wise does not offer WST accounts and will require an FSA letter of good standing plus certified director ID; Stripe accepts Samoa-registered International Companies on its Rest-of-World program and remits USD via ACH/wire to the BSP Samoa USD account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: CBS-regulated banks mandate an in-person interview at the Apia branch for at least one director and the ultimate beneficial owner before account opening; fully digital remote onboarding is not permitted under the FIU Customer Due Diligence Directive. A hybrid protocol is allowed: the director may be interviewed by secure video link only if a licensed corporate service provider in the director's country of residence performs physical identity verification and couriers a notarized certificate of identity to the Apia branch; additionally, the Samoa-registered agent must co-sign all account opening forms, and the FSA-issued certificate of incorporation and good-standing certificate must be submitted in original or duly certified copy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque shareholding structure or nominee-shareholders arrangement typical of an International Company
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chain-of-title shareholding diagram, executed declarations of trust for all nominee positions, the FSA-licensed registered agent's client due-diligence file, notarized passports of every ultimate beneficial owner, and a banker's reference from the incorporating agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: B2B SaaS small-ticket, high-velocity cross-border card receivables flagged as retail money-laundering or suspicious transactional patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed enterprise subscription agreements, itemized annual invoices, Stripe settlement metadata showing merchant category and recurring billing cycles, the ISIC 6201 software-licensing scope confirmation, and board resolutions ratifying Stripe and Wise as approved payment processors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-screening hits triggered by customer IP addresses, end-customer countries, or processor routing jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and export-control attestation, a pre-approved customer-country whitelist aligned with Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs guidance, the CBS/FIU sanctions-screening report, and contractual covenants requiring all SaaS clients to pass US, EU, Australian, and Samoan sanctions filters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance or tax-transparency justification for an offshore treasury structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FSA Economic Substance Declaration confirming non-resident management and control, shareholder tax-residency certificates, audited financial statements evidencing arm's-length back-to-back SaaS contracts, board minutes showing board meetings held outside Samoa, and CRS/FATCA registration status reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders execute a SWIFT MT103 wire to the IC's USD Capital Escrow Account at BSP Samoa, routed through BSP's New York correspondent (e.g., Bank of New York Mellon), using the CBS purpose code 'Equity Capital Contribution – Foreign Direct Investment' and the IC registration number in field 72 narrative. The authorized dealer requires the FSA certificate of good standing, certified board resolution approving the share issuance, a source-of-funds statement with six months of shareholder bank statements, and completion of CBS Form EX-26 for any injection above USD 10,000. A USD-only capital injection into an IC foreign-currency account requires no CBS prior approval; WST conversion or on-lending to any Samoan resident is prohibited under the International Companies Act, and the capital funds must remain segregated until the share allotment is filed with the FSA.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational treasury disbursements for cloud infrastructure, subprocessors, and vendor licences are executed via SWIFT MT103 from the BSP Samoa USD operational account; intra-group transfers between the IC's own accounts at different banks use MT202 straight-through-processing messages. Procurement involving physical hardware or co-location infrastructure is supported by a Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) issued by BSP Samoa with the SaaS master agreement and pro-forma invoice as the underlying trade documents. Receivables collected via Stripe_Billing are batched daily into the USD operating account, while Wise_B2B executes vendor payouts via US ACH/Fedwire and returns MT103 copies to the treasury team for netting, fee reconciliation, and CBS quarterly outflow reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/WST non-deliverable forward (NDF) with a licensed authorized dealer, tenors up to 12 months, CBS notification required – permitted for covering incidental Samoan regulatory costs
Deliverable outright forwards and FX swaps in USD/AUD, USD/NZD, and USD/EUR with the authorized dealer where the IC holds the corresponding foreign currency
Cross-currency swap (USD principal exchange with WST notional leg) executed under an approved ISDA 2002 master agreement and board treasury policy
Vanilla FX options purchased on a long-only basis (no naked short positions) with approved counterparties under the enterprise treasury management policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government License Renewal Fee and Continued Registration Declaration (USD 150 standard tier for authorized capital ≤ USD 10,000; tiered fees above)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa — lodged exclusively through the licensed Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the anniversary of incorporation (anniversary month; no residence-based fiscal year applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment within the prescribed grace period attracts a surcharge of up to 50% of the annual fee; continuing non-payment beyond the statutory period triggers suspension of the company's license and administrative strike-off from the International Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register Confirmation and Accuracy Representation (annual renewal annexure)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (register available on demand for inspection by the Samoa Registrar and Financial Intelligence Unit; no public UBO filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Delivered to the Registered Agent together with the annual renewal payment on the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unverified or stale UBO data blocks the agent's issuance of the annual renewal acknowledgment and exposes the company and each responsible officer to statutory fines; continued breach is an enforcement trigger for the Registrar.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Continued Registered Agent and Registered Office Attestation (renewal certificate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL (attestation filed by the Registered Agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed with the annual fee in the anniversary month; updated within 30 days of any change in agent or registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An International Company that is without a licensed Registered Agent or Registered Office in Samoa for more than the statutory period may be struck off by the Registrar without further reference to members.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None. International Companies are exempt from statutory audit and from any audit threshold; audit applies only if the Articles of Association mandate it or the Registrar exercises investigative powers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) recommended; no financial statements, audited or unaudited, are filed with the Samoa Registrar. Accounting records must give a true and fair view of transactions and financial position.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each annual renewal, the Registered Agent must re-verify and re-confirm the confidential Beneficial Ownership Register. All share transfers executed during the year must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the updated UBO declaration to the Agent; the declaration is provided to the Samoa Registrar and Financial Intelligence Unit only on lawful request and is not a public filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders) with transfer ledger
Register of Charges (mortgages and security interests)
Minute Book of Board and Member Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required — USD 0 (voluntary review for banking or investor purposes: USD 3,000 – 8,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (International Companies are statutorily exempt from Samoa corporate income tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Permanent zero-rate regime under the International Companies Act. The IC is exempt from income tax, withholding tax, stamp duty and exchange control on its offshore B2B SaaS revenue. No tax holiday or preferential deduction is required; the only annual state charges are the Government fee and registrar fee based on authorised capital, not on income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Not applicable: no Samoa corporate income tax return is filed for an International Company. Registry compliance consists of an annual return lodged with the Registrar of International Companies via the licensed registered agent or portal of the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual registry return only; no tax reporting frequency (no provisional tax payments, no annual tax return).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No tax filing deadline applies. The annual registry return is lodged each year within the anniversary window (generally the month of incorporation anniversary) as advised by the registered agent; the exact date is governed by the International Companies Act and the terms of the agent's engagement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: N/A (no tax form exists for an exempt IC)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: There are no income-tax fields. The annual registry filing identifies the company name, registration number, registered office/agent, share capital, director and shareholder register status, and payment of the annual fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners need not report any SaaS revenue or Samoan-source income. The registered agent should certify the IC does not carry on business with Samoa residents and does not own land or engage in licensed onshore activity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: No tax return penalty can apply because no return is due. Failure to deliver the annual registry return or pay the annual Government fee triggers a fixed late-payment penalty and, after repeated default, strike-off from the International Companies register. Registered agent non-compliance additionally attracts AML fines imposed by the Financial Intelligence Unit.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for dividends paid by an International Company to non-resident shareholders (statutory exemption; no Samoa dividend withholding tax is imposed).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No treaty relief is needed because the domestic rate is zero. Samoa has no comprehensive double-tax agreement applicable to IC dividends; a Tax Residency Certificate is not issued to a tax-exempt IC, and the dividend is outside the Samoa tax net. If a shareholder claims treaty benefits in its own jurisdiction, the protocol requires a tax residence certificate from that residence state and a reduced-rate claim under the applicable treaty; Samoa imposes no administrative requirement for this outbound distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory for outbound royalties and interest paid by an International Company; 0% for inbound royalties and interest received by the IC. Because the exemption is domestic and no DTA is invoked for this IC, no treaty-reduced rate is separately claimed.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: N/A (no Samoa transfer-pricing filing threshold applies to a tax-exempt International Company; the TP documentation obligation arises only for entities within the Samoa income tax net and is measured in Samoan tala SAT).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa does not apply domestic Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) to ordinary International Companies, and no Samoan substance filing is required solely by the ICA. Nonetheless, the IC must maintain a registered agent and registered office in Samoa for good standing. Foreign tax authorities will apply their own substance doctrines: a B2B SaaS IC that holds invoicing and intangibles without employees, business premises, economic risk or active management is likely to be recharacterised as a shell or conduit, causing foreign CFC/GILTI, permanent establishment or general anti-avoidance adjustments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / abuse of the International Company exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC carries on trade in Samoa, maintains a local physical business presence, or receives revenue from Samoan residents while continuing to claim zero-tax exempt status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of the exemption; the Revenue assesses the IC as if it were a locally taxable company on the full profits derived through Samoa, adds a shortfall penalty (up to 150% of the underpaid tax for wilful conduct) plus statutory late payment interest, and may seek deregistration for non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or submitted false certifications can be made personally liable for the unpaid tax through veil-piercing, barred from managing any Samoa entity, and prosecuted criminally for false declaration where fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / absence of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Samoan IC invoices cross-border B2B SaaS subscriptions without a Samoa office, personnel, board minutes, risk-bearing capacity or substantive contract administration, serving purely as a tax conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Samoa itself imposes no tax; however, the U.S., EU and other foreign tax authorities may recharacterise the arrangements, reattribute the SaaS/embedded-licence profit under CFC/GILTI or business profits provisions, and impose accuracy-related penalties of 20%-40% plus interest. The arrangement may also trigger secondary transfer-pricing adjustments on inventory/IP transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executives of the foreign parent group are at risk of personal penalty certifications, foreign criminal tax exposure, personal civil liability for tax collection, and travel restrictions where charges of tax evasion are filed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / KYC non-compliance and undisclosed beneficial ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The ultimate beneficial owner is concealed; the registered agent is not supplied with complete KYC/CDD documentation on the SaaS counterparties; or payments are channelled through Stripe/Wise to cryptocurrency or high-risk accounts without source-of-funds verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Office of the Financial Intelligence Unit can impose freezing orders and monetary penalties on the IC; the licensed agent can be fined and suspended; persistent violations result in deregistration and reporting to the Samoa Police.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who obstruct KYC or knowingly use the IC to launder subscription revenue are guilty of an offence under the AMLCFT Act 2007; on conviction they face fine and imprisonment, in addition to disqualification from acting as directors and personal confiscation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False annual returns and fraudulent invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC files an annual registry return claiming full inactivity while simultaneously invoicing active SaaS licence fees; or invoices for services/software that were never in substance supplied, and the registered agent certifies the false status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: False statements to the Registrar constitute an offence under the International Companies Act; penalties include fines, compulsory strike-off, and repayment of any fees or distributions made while the condition existed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for fraudulent trading: directors are personally liable for consequential losses and are subject to restitution orders, disqualification, travel bans, and imprisonment where fraud is established.
